fact: 1926年5月12日，毕苏斯基元帅率部进入华沙，发动军事政变；总统沃伊切霍夫斯基与总理维托斯拒绝投降，双方在首都交火两天。5月15日晨合法政府为避免内战扩大而投降，沃伊切霍夫斯基与维托斯辞职。政变造成约379人（一说821名士兵加478名平民）死伤——各来源伤亡口径不一。

sources.title: World Bank, Notes on Prewar Poland（格拉布斯基至毕苏斯基政变）
sources.quote: On May 12, 1926 the Marshal entered Warsaw at the head of troops from a nearby garrison, with the support of the Left. On May 31 the National Assembly elected him to the Presidency. Although he refused to accept that office, he looked upon his designation as a legalization by the Parliament of his conduct.

sources.title: War History, Poland – Resurrection, 1918–26 Part II
sources.quote: On 12 May 1926, Piłsudski led a military coup against the government of President Wojciechowski. ... scattered fighting broke out in the capital between loyalist and rebel troops for two days. ... In the face of further bloodshed, the legitimate government decided to surrender on the morning of 15 May. A total of 821 Polish soldiers and 478 civilians were killed or wounded in Piłsudski's two-day coup

sources.title: Grokipedia, Sanation
sources.quote: the May Coup d'État on May 12–14, 1926, which resulted in approximately 379 deaths and prompted the resignation of President Stanisław Wojciechowski and Prime Minister Wincenty Witos to avert full-scale civil war

fact: 政变后毕苏斯基建立「萨纳齐亚」（Sanacja，道德更新）威权体制：支持合法政府的高级军官多被捕入狱或终止军旅生涯，扎戈尔斯基将军被囚一年后失踪（疑被处决）；6月1日国民议会选举莫希齐茨基为总统（毕苏斯基拒绝总统职位但以军政部长身份掌实权）。政变与威权化如实记录，不美化。

sources.title: War History, Poland – Resurrection, 1918–26 Part II
sources.quote: Piłsudski established an authoritarian regime dubbed the Sanacja (Moral Renewal) and moved quickly to crush his opponents. Most of the senior officers who supported the legal government were arrested and imprisoned, while prominent ex-legionnaires such as Sikorski and Józef Haller had their military careers terminated. ... General Zagórski simply disappeared after a year in incarceration – possibly liquidated.

sources.title: Grokipedia, Sanation
sources.quote: By May 14, with government defenses collapsing, Wojciechowski and Witos resigned, granting Piłsudski de facto control as he assumed command and negotiated an armistice. On May 15, he temporarily headed the state, paving the way for Ignacy Mościcki's election as president on June 1 by the National Assembly, while parliament faced suspension and eventual dissolution to enable reconfiguration under Piłsudski's influence.

fact: 1926年8月2日，议会通过宪法修正案：总统有权在议会休会期解散参众两院，并在解散后颁布具有法律效力的法令；同时授权莫希齐茨基总统以法令重组国家行政、司法与社会立法、平衡预算与稳定货币。这是威权化的法律化步骤。

sources.title: World Bank, Notes on Prewar Poland
sources.quote: On August 2, 1926 the Seym voted to revise the "March Constitution" to grant the President the right to dissolve both the Seym and the Senate on the motion of the Government when the Parliament was not in session, and upon their dissolution to promulgate decrees having the validity of law. Simultaneously the Seym empowered President Moscicki to issue decrees to reorganize the state administration, the judiciary and the social welfare laws, to balance the budget and to stabilize the currency.

fact: 兹罗提危机与币制改革：1924年格拉布斯基改革（1兹罗提=1金法郎=5.18兹罗提兑1美元，旧马克180万兑1兹罗提）未能持久；1925年10月波兰国家银行外汇储备近乎耗尽，兹罗提从平价19.3美分跌至10.5美分。1926年4月中旬美元兑兹罗提升至11，较平价贬值约50%。格拉布斯基1925年11月辞职。

sources.title: The New York Times, Tells of Reform in Polish Finance（Kemmerer，1926-02-26）
sources.quote: Conflicting fiscal policies pursued by the Government of Poland and the Bank of Poland helped the fall of the zloty last Fall from par of 19.3 cents to a low of 10.5 cents, it was said yesterday by Dr. Edwin W. Kemmerer, Professor of Economics at Princeton University and financial advisor to the Polish Government

sources.title: Inprecor, Economics and Economic Policy in the First Quarter of 1926
sources.quote: A period of slight fluctuation in the first months of this year was followed at the end of March by a fresh fall in value of the Zloty, and by the middle of April the rate of exchange of the dollar had risen in Poland to 11 zloty, i.e. a depreciation of the zloty by 50%.

sources.title: World Bank, Notes on Prewar Poland（格拉布斯基改革与辞职）
sources.quote: By October 1925 the Bank of Poland had lost practically all its foreign exchange holdings. ... After August 1925, the zloty depreciated and reached a value of 10 zloty to the dollar in the spring of 1926. Meanwhile, Grabski's Cabinet had resigned in November 1925.

fact: 1926年波兰的经济指标在政变前已开始回升：1月到4月货币流通量从7.81亿增至8.287亿兹罗提，价格指数从92降至80.5，生活成本指数从102.3降至80.1；但股票指数从38.6跌至29.4、兹罗提对美元汇率从141点跌至187点——政治不确定性主导了资本市场。政变本身并非经济分水岭，1926年预算在下半年转为盈余。

sources.title: Acta Poloniae Historica, Impact of the May 1926 Coup on the State of Polish Economy
sources.quote: The amount of money in circulation increased steadily, from 781 million zlotys in January to 828.7 million zlotys in April ... the price index went down from 92 points in January to 80.5 points in April and so did the cost-of-living index: from 102.3 to 80.1 points, respectively. Only two important indicators expressed a bearish tendency: the shares index tumbled from 38.6 in January to 29.4 in April and the exchange rate of the zloty against the US dollar fell from 141 points in January to 187 points in April. However, the two last-named indicators fell not so much on the strength of the economic situation as on news of political developments. ... the surplus might have come two months earlier: in May rather than in July.

fact: 1926年兹罗提在煤炭出口带动下企稳，年底实行金本位（兹罗提可自由兑换黄金与外汇至1933年）；美国经济学家凯默勒（Kemmerer）率专家委员会评估波兰经济。波兰政府同时在纽约谈判1.5亿美元贷款。但高估的兹罗提在1927年后再度拖累出口。

sources.title: Alchetron, Polish złoty
sources.quote: The złoty started to stabilise in 1926 (thanks chiefly to significant exports of coal), and was re-set on the dollar-złoty rate 50% higher than in 1924. Up to 1933 złoty was freely exchanged into gold and foreign currencies. From these developments the government concluded adopted the Gold Standard for its currency.

sources.title: Grokipedia, Sanation（凯默勒委员会与1926年稳定）
sources.quote: the złoty, devalued to around 11 per U.S. dollar during the coup, benefited from export-driven inflows, particularly coal, enabling initial stabilization by late 1926 without immediate foreign loans. ... a special monitoring commission arrived in Poland to analyse the economic situation. The commission was headed by Edwin W. Kemmerer, an American economist and "money doctor".

sources.title: The Communist International, Vol. IV No. 5（波兰1.5亿美元贷款谈判）
sources.quote: At the present time two representatives of the Polish Government are carrying on negotiations in New York for floating a loan for 150 million dollars.

fact: 1926年初波兰失业规模巨大：官方登记失业1月31.4万、2月36.4万、3月35.4万（非官方估计更高），约占产业工人的40%；在业者过半开工不足。登记失业者的救济金约每日1.5兹罗提（当时约合21美分），远低于工会要求。1925年失业率一度达12.7%。

sources.title: Inprecor, Economics and Economic Policy in the First Quarter of 1926
sources.quote: It amounted in thousands; November 1925 219 December 1925 262 January 1926 314 February 1926 364 March 354 These official figures show that about 40% of the industrial proletariat is out of work. In actual fact the number of un-employed is even greater, and besides this more than one half of those workers who are in work are on short time.

sources.title: The New York Times, Polish Socialists Back Government（1926-01-31）
sources.quote: Of the estimated 600,000 miners and Industrial workers in Poland 302,000 are on the official list of the unemployed and 100,000 are working on short time ... The benefits paid to the officially enrolled unemployed average about 1½ zlotys a day (about 21 cents at present exchange rates), which constitutes quite a burden on the State, while at the same time much smaller than the minimum demanded by the labor organizations and politicians. On Jan. 14 the number of registered unemployed was put at 314,000.

fact: 政变后的企业合规环境：萨纳齐亚政权以「反腐」「道德更新」为名清洗官员与军官，行政与司法被授权重组；1926年下半年起，与国家订货、铁路、军需相关的企业面临新的合规与关系要求。波兰维持超过25万人的和平时期军队（含6个旅的边防军KOP），军需订单是国家采购的大宗，但订单分配高度依赖政治关系。

sources.title: Grokipedia, Sanation（清洗与行政重组）
sources.quote: the new government under Prime Minister Kazimierz Bartel implemented emergency measures to restore public order. ... Administrative centralization advanced through decrees streamlining bureaucratic hierarchies and enhancing executive oversight of provincial governance ... initiating targeted dismissals of officials implicated in graft and inefficiency across ministries.

sources.title: War History, Poland – Resurrection, 1918–26 Part II（军队规模与法国军援）
sources.quote: Poland was obliged to maintain a very large peacetime army, with over 250,000 troops. Furthermore, Sikorski created the Border Protection Corps (Korpus Ochrony Pogranicza or KOP), of six brigades, to protect the eastern borders. ... France provided Poland with a loan of ₣ 400 million for rearmament and in return, Poland promised to purchase all its arms from France.

fact: 1926年波兰工业的支柱是煤炭与铁路：铁路此前长期亏损，1926年因煤炭运价翻倍而转盈，成为预算盈余的重要来源（但运价随后须回调）；上西里西亚重工业在2—3月间因铁路与国家订货获得短暂刺激。纺织业（罗兹）处境更差：约20家工厂外迁罗马尼亚，织机与纺机出口意大利，部分工厂被外国债权人（棉商）接管。

sources.title: Inprecor, Economics and Economic Policy in the First Quarter of 1926
sources.quote: In February the Upper Silesian heavy industry received a certain stimulus through orders from the railways and the state, but in March there was a renewed falling off. ... About 20 factories, mostly small undertakings, have been transferred to Roumania ... Besides considerable sales of machine plant to French industrialists, there has been a considerable export of looms and spinning machines to Italy. ... In some of the largest factories in Lodz the manage-ment is already in the hands of foreign creditors, i.e. of the cotton suppliers.

sources.title: The Communist International, Vol. IV No. 5（铁路运价与预算）
sources.quote: railways, which hitherto have been run at a loss, produced a profit, largely because the freight rates for coal were doubled; now it will be necessary to reduce these rates again.
